place:629.title: Romer Hell's Kitchen
place:629.summary: Romer Hell's Kitchen, at 851 Eighth Ave., New York, NY 10019, is a design-led Midtown West hotel that guests praise for an easy walk to the theaters, very comfortable beds, quiet rooms and a fun piano bar. The one consistent complaint is tight bathrooms and showers.
place:629.longDetails: Romer Hell's Kitchen is a 295-room, design-led four-star hotel at 851 Eighth Avenue that took over a former Hampton Inn just west of Broadway, so Times Square, the Theater District, MoMA and Fifth Avenue are an easy walk while the side streets feel calmer. Rooms run up to 600 square feet with a fridge and city views; the all-day Neighborhood Café, a lobby study, the Corner Store and So & So's piano bar with nightly live entertainment fill the ground floor, and instead of a gym guests get free Crunch Fitness passes and bikes. Booking.com guests score it 8.6 and its location 9.6, praising friendly, helpful staff, super-comfortable beds and quiet, well-soundproofed rooms. It suits theatregoers, families and groups; the watch-out is cramped bathrooms and showers.

place:674.title: Rosa Mexicano - Lincoln Center
place:674.summary: Rosa Mexicano - Lincoln Center has moved from 61 Columbus Ave to a new flagship on the mezzanine of the Empire Hotel at 44 W 63rd Street, with expanded dining areas and multiple bars. The draw is theater-adjacent fun and the signature tableside guacamole. Reviews are mixed, with Tripadvisor travelers praising the look and staff yet flagging uneven service and some weaker mains, so treat it as a lively, convenient pre-show choice.
place:674.longDetails: The new space sits across from the Metropolitan Opera House, which suits a pre-show meal. Fiesta Hour runs Monday to Friday, 4–7 pm, in the bar area, and Taco Tuesdays bring half-price tacos all day (dine-in only). place:695.title: Cafe Luxembourg
place:695.summary: Cafe Luxembourg is the Upper West Side brasserie people return to around Lincoln Center performances, a polished but relaxed room of regulars where service is consistently praised. Good neighborhood spot, conveniently close to Lincoln Center sums up its appeal, and the steak au poivre and house-made ice cream are the orders to remember.
place:695.longDetails: Cafe Luxembourg has been a fixture of the neighborhood, a classic Upper West Side American brasserie since 1983 serving American classics with a nod to French cooking a short walk from Lincoln Center. Its strongest identity is timing: diners recommend it before or after a play or ballet, and the room fills with regulars and performance-goers. The kitchen gets steady praise (“The steak au poivre is delicious”), and Restaurantji shows 4.3 from 1186 ratings. Expect a loud, busy room at curtain times and prices that match its institution status, so reserve and leave time before a show.
